title: Conformation et proportions des parties du corps de l'adulte
author: N. H. Jacob (drawn from nature), lith. J. Bénard
work: Bourgery & Jacob, Traité complet de l'anatomie de l'homme — Atlas I
note: Five contour figures — male and female, front and profile — drawn against TWO printed rulers: a centesimal scale (percent of stature) and an absolute scale in French inches. Landmark letters key each level to both. This is the measured proportional canon the anatomy program was missing on disk: read a landmark height off the centesimal rule and it transfers to any stature.

title: Sujet complet de syndesmologie — plan antérieur
author: N. H. Jacob (drawn from nature), lith. J. Bénard
work: Bourgery & Jacob, Traité complet de l'anatomie de l'homme — Atlas I
note: One skeleton standing in a relaxed asymmetric stance with EVERY ligament left in place, numbered 1–27+. The joint-graph in a single image: each articulation is both located in the body and named. Note the ligaments read as pale strapping that visually fuses adjacent bone ends — joints are volumes, not pivots.

title: Sujet complet de syndesmologie — plan postérieur
author: N. H. Jacob (drawn from nature), lith. J. Bénard
work: Bourgery & Jacob, Traité complet de l'anatomie de l'homme — Atlas I
note: The posterior counterpart to pl. 44, same subject and numbering — so the two plates register against each other for a full 360° ligament survey.

title: Articulations rachidiennes et costo-vertébrales
author: N. H. Jacob (drawn from nature), lith. J. Bénard
work: Bourgery & Jacob, Traité complet de l'anatomie de l'homme — Atlas I
note: Whole spine with its ligaments, anterior and posterior, plus the rib-to-vertebra joints — the chain that decides how a torso bends and how a ribcage rides on it.

title: Articulations céphalo-rachidiennes
author: N. H. Jacob (drawn from nature), lith. J. Bénard
work: Bourgery & Jacob, Traité complet de l'anatomie de l'homme — Atlas I
note: Skull-to-spine junction at life size: occiput, atlas and axis with the ligaments that let a head nod and rotate on two different joints. The head's two-axis pivot, drawn.

title: Articulations rachidiennes, 7e à 12e vertèbre dorsale
author: N. H. Jacob (drawn from nature), lith. J. Bénard
work: Bourgery & Jacob, Traité complet de l'anatomie de l'homme — Atlas I
note: Thoracic segment in isolation — disc, facet and ligament detail for the least mobile stretch of the spine.

title: Articulations rachidiennes, 2e à 4e vertèbre lombaire
author: N. H. Jacob (drawn from nature), lith. J. Bénard
work: Bourgery & Jacob, Traité complet de l'anatomie de l'homme — Atlas I
note: Lumbar segment at life size: the thick discs and heavy ligaments that carry the trunk's load, drawn large enough to model from.

title: Articulations temporo-maxillaire, sterno-claviculaires, chondro-sternales et chondro-costales
author: N. H. Jacob (drawn from nature), lith. J. Bénard
work: Bourgery & Jacob, Traité complet de l'anatomie de l'homme — Atlas I
note: Jaw hinge, the sternoclavicular joint, and the cartilage joints of the rib cage on one sheet — the three articulations most often faked in game rigs.

title: Articulations pelviennes et coxo-fémorales
author: N. H. Jacob (drawn from nature), lith. J. Bénard
work: Bourgery & Jacob, Traité complet de l'anatomie de l'homme — Atlas I
note: Whole pelvis, front and back, ligaments intact: sacroiliac, the sacrotuberous/sacrospinous straps, and both hip capsules. The pelvis reads as one strapped ring, not three bones.

title: Articulations pelviennes et coxo-fémorale — grandeur naturelle
author: N. H. Jacob (drawn from nature), lith. J. Bénard
work: Bourgery & Jacob, Traité complet de l'anatomie de l'homme — Atlas I
note: Life-size hip: the joint opened and sectioned so the socket, the capsule and the ligamentum teres are all visible at true scale.

title: Articulations scapulo-claviculaire, scapulo-humérale et huméro-cubitale
author: N. H. Jacob (drawn from nature), lith. J. Bénard
work: Bourgery & Jacob, Traité complet de l'anatomie de l'homme — Atlas I
note: The shoulder girdle as a linkage — clavicle to scapula to humerus — with the elbow as small companion figures. Where the arm actually attaches to the body.

title: Articulations huméro-cubitale et radio-carpienne
author: N. H. Jacob (drawn from nature), lith. J. Bénard
work: Bourgery & Jacob, Traité complet de l'anatomie de l'homme — Atlas I
note: Elbow at half scale and wrist at life size, in several rotations each — enough views to reconstruct both joints' swing limits.

title: Articulations de la main — grandeur naturelle
author: N. H. Jacob (drawn from nature), lith. J. Bénard
work: Bourgery & Jacob, Traité complet de l'anatomie de l'homme — Atlas I
note: Two life-size hands, dorsal and palmar, ligaments in place, plus two sagittal finger sections. The modelling truth here: the carpal ligament mass is a dense white block that HIDES the individual carpals — a wrist reads as one strapped lump, and the metacarpal heads are tied to each other by transverse bands.

title: Articulations du genou, fémoro-tibiale, rotulienne et péronéo-tibiale supérieure
author: N. H. Jacob (drawn from nature), lith. J. Bénard
work: Bourgery & Jacob, Traité complet de l'anatomie de l'homme — Atlas I
note: Nine figures of one knee: anterior, posterior, both laterals, flexed, a sagittal section showing cruciates and cancellous bone interior, and two plateau views drawn from above with the MENISCI in place. A complete single-joint kit — every view a rigger needs plus the section that explains it.

title: Articulations péronéo-tibiales et tibio-tarsienne
author: N. H. Jacob (drawn from nature), lith. J. Bénard
work: Bourgery & Jacob, Traité complet de l'anatomie de l'homme — Atlas I
note: Ankle and the tibia–fibula pairing at life size: the mortise the talus sits in, and the membrane binding the two leg bones along their whole length.

title: Ligamens du pied
author: N. H. Jacob (drawn from nature), lith. J. Bénard
work: Bourgery & Jacob, Traité complet de l'anatomie de l'homme — Atlas I
note: Two dorsal feet at life size with the ligament sheet intact — the strapping that turns a pile of tarsals into an arch.

title: Articulations et ligamens profonds du pied
author: N. H. Jacob (drawn from nature), lith. J. Bénard
work: Bourgery & Jacob, Traité complet de l'anatomie de l'homme — Atlas I
note: The deep layer: plantar and lateral views showing the ligaments that actually carry the arch once the superficial sheet is stripped.

title: Sujet complet de myologie — plan antérieur
author: N. H. Jacob (drawn from nature), lith. J. Bénard
work: Bourgery & Jacob, Traité complet de l'anatomie de l'homme — Atlas II (Myologie)
note: The muscular twin of the syndesmology figure: one standing body, every superficial muscle in place, numbered throughout. Colour-printed, so contractile muscle and tendon read apart at a glance.

title: Sujet complet de myologie — plan postérieur
author: N. H. Jacob (drawn from nature), lith. J. Bénard
work: Bourgery & Jacob, Traité complet de l'anatomie de l'homme — Atlas II (Myologie)
note: Posterior counterpart, same subject and numbering — the two register for a full survey of the surface muscle layer.

title: Ensemble des muscles du tronc — couche superficielle
author: N. H. Jacob (drawn from nature), lith. J. Bénard
work: Bourgery & Jacob, Traité complet de l'anatomie de l'homme — Atlas II (Myologie)
note: The colour is load-bearing: red-brown = contractile belly, pale grey = aponeurosis. Read the abdomen and it is mostly PALE — the front of the belly is a broad tendon sheet, not muscle, with red only out at the flank. Note also that Bourgery dissects the two halves to DIFFERENT DEPTHS, so one figure carries two layers: pectoralis intact on one side, serratus digitations interleaving with the oblique on the other.

title: Paroi antérieure du tronc — muscles de la première couche
author: N. H. Jacob (drawn from nature), lith. J. Bénard
work: Bourgery & Jacob, Traité complet de l'anatomie de l'homme — Atlas II (Myologie)
note: First layer of the anterior trunk wall. Start of a four-plate strip-down: build a torso by following the sequence outward-in, or inward-out.

title: Paroi antérieure du tronc — muscles de la deuxième couche
author: N. H. Jacob (drawn from nature), lith. J. Bénard
work: Bourgery & Jacob, Traité complet de l'anatomie de l'homme — Atlas II (Myologie)
note: Second layer. The same body, one stratum deeper — the value is the registration between plates, not any single sheet.

title: Paroi antérieure du tronc — muscles de la troisième couche
author: N. H. Jacob (drawn from nature), lith. J. Bénard
work: Bourgery & Jacob, Traité complet de l'anatomie de l'homme — Atlas II (Myologie)
note: Third layer, ribs beginning to show through. The end of the strip-down, where muscle gives way to skeleton.

title: Muscles de l'avant-bras
author: N. H. Jacob (drawn from nature), lith. J. Bénard
work: Bourgery & Jacob, Traité complet de l'anatomie de l'homme — Atlas II (Myologie)
note: Forearm in three rotations plus two detail figures — the bellies that drive the hand, shown where they actually sit.

title: Muscles de la main — couche superficielle, grandeur naturelle
author: N. H. Jacob (drawn from nature), lith. J. Bénard
work: Bourgery & Jacob, Traité complet de l'anatomie de l'homme — Atlas II (Myologie)
note: Life-size palm, and the lesson is where the red ISN'T: muscle sits only in the thenar and hypothenar eminences and the lumbricals, while the FINGERS CONTAIN NO MUSCLE AT ALL — pale tendon and sheath the whole way out. Finger power is imported from the forearm. The cut stump at the wrist shows that import as a bundle of pale cords in section.

title: Muscles de la paume de la main — couche profonde
author: N. H. Jacob (drawn from nature), lith. J. Bénard
work: Bourgery & Jacob, Traité complet de l'anatomie de l'homme — Atlas II (Myologie)
note: Deep palm with sectional figures — the interossei layer under the long tendons.

title: Muscles de la main — plan postérieur
author: N. H. Jacob (drawn from nature), lith. J. Bénard
work: Bourgery & Jacob, Traité complet de l'anatomie de l'homme — Atlas II (Myologie)
note: Back of the hand: extensor tendons fanning over the metacarpals with almost no muscle belly to hide them.

title: Muscles pelvi-fémoraux — couche superficielle, grandeur naturelle
author: N. H. Jacob (drawn from nature), lith. J. Bénard
work: Bourgery & Jacob, Traité complet de l'anatomie de l'homme — Atlas II (Myologie)
note: Life-size gluteal mass as a single sweeping sheet — the body's largest muscle drawn big enough to see its fibre direction change across its width.

title: Muscles pelvi-fémoraux — deuxième couche
author: N. H. Jacob (drawn from nature), lith. J. Bénard
work: Bourgery & Jacob, Traité complet de l'anatomie de l'homme — Atlas II (Myologie)
note: Gluteus maximus removed: the deep rotators exposed as a fan converging on the greater trochanter. The hip's steering layer.

title: Muscles de la cuisse — plan antérieur, couche superficielle
author: N. H. Jacob (drawn from nature), lith. J. Bénard
work: Bourgery & Jacob, Traité complet de l'anatomie de l'homme — Atlas II (Myologie)
note: Anterior thigh, superficial layer — quadriceps group and the sartorius crossing it diagonally.

title: Cou — anatomie chirurgicale, grandeur naturelle
author: N. H. Jacob (drawn from nature), lith. Bénard & Frey
work: Bourgery & Jacob, Traité complet de l'anatomie de l'homme — Atlas VI (Anatomie chirurgicale)
note: Two life-size neck dissections on a TRUE BLACK ground, and the black is the technique: the specimen floats free, so a pale subject reads at maximum clarity. Colour does the labelling — blue veins, orange arteries, white nerve cords, red muscle, cream bone and fascia, a legend without a legend. Note the borders: they are drawn as CUT EDGES, skin showing as a brown rind, so the plate reads as an excised block with real depth, not a floating diagram.

title: Plans musculaires, aponévroses, vaisseaux et nerfs du périnée
author: N. H. Jacob (drawn from nature), lith. Bénard & Frey
work: Bourgery & Jacob, Traité complet de l'anatomie de l'homme — Atlas VI (Anatomie chirurgicale)
note: The pelvic floor in layers — the region games never model and always get wrong when a body is viewed from below.

title: Intérieur de la cavité du bassin — grandeur naturelle
author: N. H. Jacob (drawn from nature), lith. Bénard & Frey
work: Bourgery & Jacob, Traité complet de l'anatomie de l'homme — Atlas VI (Anatomie chirurgicale)
note: A life-size horizontal section through the pelvis on black. Read it for how body mass is actually distributed in the hips — the bone ring is a thin shell around a large soft volume.

title: Loges musculaires des régions lombaire, fessière et fémorale postérieure
author: N. H. Jacob (drawn from nature), lith. Bénard & Frey
work: Bourgery & Jacob, Traité complet de l'anatomie de l'homme — Atlas VI (Anatomie chirurgicale)
note: Muscle COMPARTMENTS rather than individual muscles: the fascial envelopes that bundle the back and buttock groups. The right abstraction level for a game body — bundles, not strands.

title: Loges musculaires, aponévroses, vaisseaux et nerfs du cou et de l'aisselle
author: N. H. Jacob (drawn from nature), lith. Bénard & Frey
work: Bourgery & Jacob, Traité complet de l'anatomie de l'homme — Atlas VI (Anatomie chirurgicale)
note: Neck and armpit at life size with the head thrown back — the axilla opened as the passage it really is, where the arm's supply crosses from trunk to limb.
